name: first-session
note: CE3 north-star goalpost: a beginner on a COLD device (cleared storage, the runner's fresh browser context - first-run tour has never completed) reaches a strummable chord AND HEARS it (real production audio path invoked, not a mention) within <=5 taps. Enumerated tap path (verified against play/index.html + songbook.js - the tour has no bypass, S-WELCOME 2026-08-09 note: 'the tour ENDS in a jam on EVERY path', Skip and Start-playing share one finish() handler): TAP 1 #wNext (Start playing) - picks guitar-standard, sets the one-shot music.welcomeJam.v1 flag, reloads into the featured backing-track's Studio (jam, not yet playing - honest unstarted embed, a page load is not a gesture). TAP 2 .bt-st-back - leaves the jam Studio back to the mini player / Library. TAP 3 .tabbar[data-tab=compose] - lands on Compose; unset guidance level renders the beginner-safe default (#suggest .progPick starter cards, no dense chord palette). TAP 4 #suggest .progPick (first starter, '4-chord song') - loadProgression() fills #prog with a playable progression SILENTLY (renderProg/renderKey only, no packPlayChord call) - this is CE-point (a), a strummable chord affordance now on screen: each #prog .slot renders a diagram/token whose onclick is packPlayChord(c) (songbook.js renderProg, both the 'full' <=4-chord diagram-card branch and the compact-token branch wire the same handler). TAP 5 the first #prog chord card/token - fires packPlayChord -> pack.playChord (chord-pack-adapter.js) -> window.ChordAudio.strum/tone, the SAME production Karplus-Strong synthesis entrypoint chord-chips-accessible.json's MOCK-INTEGRITY GUARD proves exists - this is CE-point (b), audio actually fired. Audio-fired assertion follows this suite's own established pattern (chord-chips-accessible.json): wrap the REAL window.ChordAudio.strum/.tone with a call-through counter immediately before the tap (so production behavior is unchanged - the wrap is instrumentation, not a stub standing in for deleted audio), assert the counter incremented from a REAL trusted click on the REAL DOM node, then restore the originals. No app-level 'played' flag/class exists for a single Compose chip tap (competency.js only records evidence for a whole composed SONG) so the production audio call IS the app's real artifact here - there is nothing else to assert against. CE-point (c), tap count <=5: exactly 5 'tap' steps below (wNext, back, compose-tab, progPick, chord-card) - verify by grep -c '"action": "tap"' on this file if the count ever needs re-proving.

steps.label: cold device: the tour has not yet been completed and greets before anything else (index.html boot unconditionally persists a resolved profile key on EVERY load, tour-shown or not, so welcomeDone - not activeProfile - is the fresh-device signal, per welcome-tour.json/persona-firsttimer-journey.json)
tap 1 lands the beginner IN a jam (the tour's own payoff) - Studio open, embed mounted, honestly unstarted
unset level (no ask fired yet) renders the beginner-safe landing: one-tap starter progressions, not a dense chord palette
CE3 (a): a strummable chord is now on screen - the starter filled #prog with playable chord cards/tokens, each wired to packPlayChord (tap-to-hear)

install the audio-fire probe: wrap the REAL ChordAudio.strum/.tone with a call-through counter (production behavior unchanged) immediately before the strum tap, per the chord-chips-accessible.json MOCK-INTEGRITY convention
CE3 (b): audio actually fired - the real production ChordAudio entrypoint was invoked by the real tap (not a mention, not a mock standing in for deleted audio); restore the originals
